summary.en-US: Lets Claude Code use your Firefox: open tabs, click, type, read pages, fill forms and take screenshots. Needs Claude Code and the companion bridge from npm. Not affiliated with Anthropic.

description.en-US:
Claude Code Bridge for Firefox lets Claude Code use your everyday Firefox. It can open tabs, click, type, read pages, fill forms, take screenshots, and read console and network logs. It works in your real profile, with your logins.

**Setup**

The add-on needs Claude Code and its companion bridge, which you install with Node 20 or newer:

`npx @llyfn/claude-in-firefox install`

Then start a new Claude Code session and ask it to use Firefox.

**What it sends, and where**

Each Claude Code session gets its own Firefox window. Claude can only read and act on the tabs in that window, plus popups opened from them. From those tabs the add-on sends page content (text, page structure, form fields, screenshots, dialog messages, console messages and network requests) and browsing activity (addresses and titles) to the bridge on your computer through Firefox native messaging. The bridge hands them to Claude Code, which sends them to Claude as part of your conversation. The add-on sends nothing to its developer.

The add-on keeps the console messages and network requests of every tab in memory. They leave Firefox only if Claude reads them from a tab in its session window, including a tab you move into that window.

Data also flows the other way: when Claude uploads a file to a page, the bridge reads the local file Claude names and the add-on attaches it to the page's file input.

**Staying in control**

Pages in a session window show a "Claude is using this window · Stop" bar. Stop blocks Claude until you press Resume; if you close the window instead, Claude can open a new one. The bar doesn't appear on about: pages, other add-ons' pages, PDFs and some restricted sites.

**Before you use it**

Claude acts as you, with your logged-in sessions, and the add-on blocks no sites. A page can contain text written to steer Claude. Read [Safety](https://github.com/llyfn/claude-in-firefox#safety) before you use it on sites that matter.
